svg.text: K9c THE HAND — printer-class Cartesian gantry under Klipper
Same kinematics as K9b (X, Z, Y, roll), built from maker-market parts with open-loop steppers.
lift ≤ 6 kg at ≤ 160 mm · roll 10 Nm · top speed 0.8 m/s (K9b 1.2)
push 300 N within y ≤ 420, 150 N at full reach (90 Nm on the X carriage)
SIDE SECTION through the hand (rear wall left, kitchen right)
X AXIS seen from the front: belt pulls the carriage on two rails
COLLISION: the load cell is the sensor

g.text: arm-root load cell: weighs and senses collisions
Y: NEMA 17 + belt on MGN12 in the arm tube
band 2 covers the slot under the tube
sleeve grips each item by its stub

svg.text: X box (dry): 40 × 80 profile, 2 × MGN15 rails, HTD belt
Z motor: NEMA 23 + 2 Nm brake (holds unpowered)
labyrinth slot, no seal (purged by under-pressure)
Z: SFU1610 ball screw inside the hanging mast
band 1: stainless strip covers the mast's Z slot
Z travel 900 mm (roll axis z 700–1600) · Y travel 450 mm · arm tube 60 × 60 stainless
labyrinth slot along the X box floor
HTD 3M-15 belt · 2 × MGN15 rails on a 40 × 80 beam, 1.4 m
open-loop NEMA 23 (3 Nm) on a TMC driver · 0.8 m/s
lever arm from the X carriage (mm)
force above threshold → Klipper halts X, Y, Z
X Y Z · roll T · S
X, Y, Z as a printer;

g.text: 1/6 X: an open-loop NEMA 23 pulls the carriage along two MGN15 rails with an HTD belt; the slot is only a labyrinth
2/6 Z: the SFU1610 ball screw in the mast lowers the arm; the brake holds it without power; band 1 covers the slot
3/6 Y: a belt inside the stainless arm tube moves the drop link forward; band 2 covers the slot under the tube
4/6 Roll: NEMA 23 + 20:1 planetary turns the sleeve through a canned magnet coupling — here: pouring
5/6 Push: open-loop motors give 90 Nm on the X carriage — 300 N close to the wall, 150 N at full reach
6/6 Collision: the arm-root load cell sees an unexpected force and Klipper halts all axes
